verses.text: So I’m asking: did God reject his people? No way! I’m an Israelite myself, Abraham’s descendant, from Benjamin’s tribe.
God hasn’t rejected the people he knew beforehand. Don’t you remember what Scripture says about Elijah, when he brought Israel’s case before God?
“Lord, they killed your prophets and tore down your altars. I’m the only one left, and now they’re trying to kill me too.”
But what did God tell him? “I’ve kept seven thousand for myself who haven’t bowed to Baal.”
It’s the same now: there’s a remnant, chosen by grace.
And if it’s grace, it’s not earned by works. Otherwise grace wouldn’t be grace. If it were earned by works, it wouldn’t be grace either.
So what happened? Israel didn’t get what they were seeking, but the chosen ones did. The rest became hardened.
Just as Scripture says, “God gave them a spirit of stupor: eyes that can’t see and ears that can’t hear, right up to this day.”
David says, “Let their table become a trap, a snare, a stumbling block, and a payback for them.”
“Let their eyes go dark so they can’t see; keep their backs bent forever.”
So did they stumble just to fall for good? Absolutely not! Their fall opened the way for salvation to reach the Gentiles, making Israel jealous.
If Israel’s fall brought riches to the world, and their loss brought riches to the Gentiles, just imagine what their full restoration will bring!
I’m speaking to you Gentiles now. Since I’m an apostle to the Gentiles, I take my ministry seriously,
hoping somehow to make my own people jealous and save some of them.
If their rejection brought the world back to God, what will their acceptance be? It’ll be like life rising from the dead!
If the first piece of dough offered to God is holy, the whole batch is holy too. If the root is holy, the branches are too.
Some branches were snapped off. You were a wild olive branch, but God grafted you in among them, so now you share the root and its rich nourishment.
So don’t brag over the branches. If you do, remember: you don’t hold up the root—the root holds you up.
You might say, “Branches were snapped off so I could be grafted in.”
That’s true: they were snapped off because they didn’t believe, and you stand through faith. Don’t get big-headed; stay in awe.
If God didn’t spare the natural branches, he won’t spare you either.
Look at both God’s kindness and his severity. He was severe toward those who fell, but kind toward you—if you keep living in his kindness. Otherwise, you too will be cut off.
And if they don’t keep going in unbelief, they’ll be grafted back in. God has the power to graft them in again.
If you were cut from a wild olive tree and grafted—against nature—into a cultivated one, how much more can the natural branches be grafted back into their own olive tree?
Family, I don’t want you missing this mystery or getting too impressed with yourselves: Israel has become partly hardened until the full number of Gentiles comes in,
and then all Israel will be saved. Scripture says, “The Rescuer will come from Zion and turn Jacob away from ungodliness.”
“This is my covenant with them: I’ll take away their sins.”
As far as the Good News goes, they’re enemies for your benefit. But as far as God’s choice goes, they’re loved because of the ancestors.
God doesn’t take back his gifts or his call. 🔒
Back then you Gentiles disobeyed God, but now you’ve received mercy through Israel’s disobedience.
In the same way, Israel has now disobeyed, so through the mercy shown to you, they too may receive mercy.
God has allowed everyone to be caught up in disobedience, so he can show mercy to everyone.
Wow—the depth of God’s riches, wisdom, and knowledge! Who can fully figure out his judgments or trace his paths?
“Who has known the Lord’s mind? Who has ever been his adviser?”
“Who gave God anything first, so God would owe them a payback?”
Everything comes from him, exists through him, and leads back to him. Give him glory forever! Amen. 🙌
